#3120. Grand Theft Auto 6 Is Out. Here’s How to Make Room on Your Console

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

You can make space on your console for GTA 6 a few different ways.

The wait is over. Grand Theft Auto 6 is out, and it is massive. The game is 212 GB, which means it takes up about half of the storage space on my Xbox Series S. The company announced that GTA 6 is available to stream via Xbox Cloud Gaming without downloading it to your console. However, cloud streaming GTA 6 might affect the game’s performance and relies heavily on a strong internet connection. To avoid those issues, I plan on downloading the game.

If you’re like me and are excited to play GTA 6 but don’t have much storage space, you have a few options: delete games, upgrade your console’s hard drive and streaming the game. Here’s what you should know about these options.

The simplest and cheapest way to free up space on your console for Grand Theft Auto 6 is to delete files and other games, which is what I’ll be doing. Uninstalling games is a good choice for folks who plan on spending a lot of time with GTA 6 and don’t intend to juggle different games. Rob Nelson, who oversees Rockstar North with Aaron Garbut, told The New York Times that he had an 80-hour playthrough of the game in February, so you can easily stay immersed in Grand Theft Auto’s state of Leonida.

You may not need to delete much – uninstalling a game like Call of Duty alone could free up nearly 315 GB, giving you enough digital storage for GTA 6. Since deleting files is almost instantaneous, you can quickly reclaim hard drive space. Because you don’t need to buy additional storage, you’ll also save a lot of money – storage prices are through the roof at the moment.

Ultimately, deleting games is a great option if you don’t want to spend any additional money or you don’t mind redownloading games later.

If you plan on hopping between GTA 6 and other games, or you don’t want to delete many of your downloaded titles, you can upgrade your console’s storage. Buying storage is more expensive than deleting files from your console, but benefit from being able to seamlessly hop between Grand Theft Auto 6 and Call of Duty or Madden.

You can use internal or external storage for your console, but you might have to move files between your internal and external storage to launch games. An internal hard drive lets you seamlessly play games. Xbox consoles rely on proprietary expansion cards from Seagate or SanDisk that plug into your console for additional storage. The PlayStation 5 uses M.2 solid-state drives, which are installed alongside the PS5’s built-in storage, and CNET’s David Carnoy recommends the Lexar NM 790 as a fast SSD with a straightforward installation process.

There shouldn’t be any performance, quality or load-time differences between running games from installed storage expansion devices versus your console’s internal storage. Both expansion cards and SSDs can be expensive, especially when compared with deleting games.

You could also use an external hard drive to expand your storage, which can be cheaper than buying expansion cards and internal SSD upgrades – you may even have a compatible USB external drive sitting around that you can use. However, there are caveats around what games can and can’t be played directly from external HDDs.

For Xbox consoles, some older Xbox, Xbox 360 and Xbox One titles can be stored and played from external HDDs. But games optimized for Series X/S consoles can only be stored on HDDs and must be moved back to your internal drive to play. Similarly, the PlayStation 5 only lets you store PS5 games on external HDDs, while you can store and run PS4 games from external drives.

Therefore, using an external HDD requires playing digital musical chairs, moving current-gen games back and forth between your external hard drive and internal console storage in order to play them. The LaCie Rugged SSD4 earned a CNET Editors’ Choice Award and could be a good option. If its price tag scares you, the Western Digital P10 offers more storage at a more economical price point.

Rockstar announced that GTA 6 is available to stream on the Xbox consoles – no download required – via Xbox Cloud Gaming, with some quality and time limitations. You’ll need to buy either an Xbox Game Pass plan or Cloud Gaming hours. Folks who don’t want to delete games or upgrade their console storage can stream GTA 6, but you’ll need an Xbox One or Series X/S console, you won’t get the highest visual quality and you will have to pay for more playtime hours if they run out. Streaming GTA 6 could help budget-conscious gamers who don’t want to upgrade from Xbox One consoles or who don’t have the allotted storage space on their devices.

Normally, you can stream many games on PCs, mobile devices and TVs or streaming devices using Xbox Cloud Gaming or Game Pass, but Grand Theft Auto 6 is limited to the Xbox One, Series S and Series X. Additionally, GTA 6 streaming quality is capped at Series S graphical settings. So if you have a Series X, consider deleting games or upgrading your storage to run the game locally with better graphics.

While you’ll need to install the full game on your console first, remote play for Xbox and PlayStation consoles lets you stream GTA 6 to other devices, like your phone, tablet, streaming device or TV.

If you’re willing to pay a little more for the convenience of having multiple games ready to play at a moment’s notice, Xbox expansion cards or an internal SSD for a PS5 are your best options. If you want a cheaper option and don’t mind moving game files around, an external hard drive could be for you. If you have Xbox Game Pass or Xbox Cloud Gaming, you could stream the game to your console without needing more storage space. However, the cheapest option is to delete games from your internal storage and redownload them later, which can be time-consuming.

I chose the cheapest option and deleted a few games from my Xbox. I’m not planning on leaving GTA 6 any time soon.

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Over one-third have already started holiday shopping, but November's sales could yield big savings.

Even though early holiday sales started months ago, shopping your wish lists during Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales may be worth the wait if you’re one of the few planning to shop November sales. It’s the time to save money on most tech devices. But holiday shopping could look different for US adults juggling smaller budgets and shopping frustrations.

CNET’s annual holiday shopping survey shows that 27% of US adults plan to start holiday shopping in November and 17% plan to shop during sales. However, US adults will be juggling a smaller tech budget of $808. That’s $123 less than CNET’s survey findings last year.

Finding savings is paramount to staying within your price range this year, but how can you spot a good deal when nearly every retailer is having a sale? CNET experts weighed in on US adults’ holiday shopping plans and shared expert advice to score the best Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals on must-haves.

CNET found that 27% will plan or start their holiday shopping this month, with 17% of November shoppers planning to shop holiday sales, like Black Friday and Cyber Monday.

The big question is whether the sales are worthwhile. CNET’s director of commerce content, Russell Holly, says it comes down to when you find a deal on a must-have item.

“The best time to buy is the moment you see something you want on an actual discount, because increased prices can come at any time,” Holly said.

Holly says even steep discounts aren’t lowering prices as much as before, but the right deals may make you reconsider. You just have to know where and when to shop for tech devices.

For example, Black Friday is usually the best time to buy electronics, including TVs and robot vacuums, with the biggest deals lasting from Black Friday to Cyber Monday.

CNET’s senior laptops editor, Matt Elliott, says if you’re planning to buy a new laptop during holiday sales, look for discounts at Amazon, Best Buy and vendor sites like Dell, HP and Lenovo.

“These retailers and companies are constantly rotating discounts on laptops, and these sales can save you hundreds of dollars. So, it’s worth tracking the price of a laptop you want and buying it when it dips,” said Elliott.

Black Friday and Cyber Monday are also a good time to buy the latest wearables, said CNET’s wearable expert, Vanessa Hand Orellana.

“For Black Friday, all the heavy wearable hitters tend to go on sale: Google, Samsung, Oura, Garmin and Apple,” said Orellana. However, if you don’t need the latest tech, you can find some of the best deals on last year’s tech at third-party retailers, like Best Buy and Walmart. And many of the previous-gen models share the same features as the newest ones, said Orellana.

CNET’s deals team spends hours making sure sales are legitimate — not just a fake price drop. And in the coming weeks, they’ll track deals on devices like laptops, headphones, wearable devices and smart home gadgets, plus alternatives to more costly tech, to help you determine what’s worth buying now or later.

You can also check an item’s price history to see if you’re getting the best deal by using price trackers like CamelCamelCamel and comparing prices across retailers before buying. But as Holly noted, if you want to upgrade your personal devices, don’t wait. Look for the best price you can find and buy it right away. Otherwise, prices may go up while you wait.

Last year, CNET found that US adults planned to spend an average of $931 on holiday shopping. This year, shoppers are planning to spend less.

On average, they expect to spend $808 on holiday shopping. That’s $123 less than last year. Some generations plan to spend more, such as millennials, who anticipate an average holiday shopping outlay of $1,074. Boomers will spend around half that amount — $582.

Higher everyday living costs could explain why holiday budgets are lower.“Everything else being more expensive means less left over for gifts,” said Holly. “There’s very little indication that component prices are going to come back down anytime soon, so if you’re hoping for the kinds of prices you saw even two years ago, I would say you’re going to be waiting quite a while.”

Balancing holiday gifts and everyday basics on your usual income can be a lot to handle. Now’s the time to set holiday expectations, including a budget and a list of must-haves, along with more affordable options that still meet your needs.

Then keep checking prices and deals from your trusted retailers and be prepared to buy when you spot good savings. Most importantly, try to avoid using credit cards and buy-now, pay-later plans that can lead to debt. The Federal Reserve’s recent rate hike held rates elevated, which means borrowing costs will remain high and make debt more expensive through higher credit card and loan interest rates.

CNET found that 73% of shoppers plan to buy tech products or services this season, but what most US adults plan to buy and how much they plan to spend may surprise you.

Thirty percent of shoppers plan to purchase toys, and 25% plan to buy kitchen items, such as air fryers and cookware. But shoppers don’t plan to buy as many personal electronics and home entertainment products. Only 20% plan to buy headphones or earbuds, and even fewer plan to buy video games for consoles (18%) or laptops and TVs (11%). More shocking is that only 13% plan to buy phones. We’ve seen prices increase across popular tech devices and brands due to the RAM shortage, which has led to low supply and high demand for memory chips.

Some of the latest releases cost way more than the average $808 most US adults plan to spend. For instance, the $2,000 iPhone Duo alone costs even more than the average $1,704 that millennials plan to spend on tech this holiday season. And less costly phones are still beyond holiday budgets, like the $1,200 iPhone 18 Pro Max, and even the iPhone 18 Pro is $1,200. Trade-in offers and sales can help lower that cost if you’re planning to upgrade, but shop around and compare deals before buying.

Increased prices may make you reconsider whether to stick with your current model or upgrade, but remember, you have options.

“If the current laptop works well enough, upgrading can either be viewed as a luxury purchase for later or shifted to buying used or refurbished models to save extra,” Holly said.

You may also consider a slightly older model of the device you’re looking for. It could still have all of the features you need, but cost less. Another money-saving option is to consider refurbished tech that’s in excellent or good condition from a certified refurbished retailer. You may still notice some price increases due to demand, but it could still cost less than the newest models.

Most US shoppers (84%) expect the holiday shopping season to come with a few hurdles this year. Forty-three percent are concerned about deceptive pricing practices, such as retailers raising original prices before discounting them for a sale. Others are concerned about deals selling out immediately because of low stock or automated buying bots (39%).

But if you’re more worried about fake deals or sales being a money grab by retailers, Holly said that historically, there have been some great sales ahead of the holidays. It’s still best to do your research before buying to make sure you’re getting a deal by comparing retailer prices before and after announced sales and using price tracking tools, like CamelCamelCamel. Heads up that many retailers, like Amazon, have flash sales with specific times of deeper discounts, and you’ll need to act fast, so it’s best to plan your holiday shopping now.

“The best thing anyone can do ahead of a shopping event is prepare,” said Holly. “Find your favorite price tracker tool before the event starts, have a general idea of what you’re looking to buy and be sure to keep an eye out for bigger discounts when you bundle things together.”

CNET commissioned YouGov Plc to conduct the survey. All figures, unless otherwise stated, are from YouGov Plc. The total sample size was 2,615 adults, of whom 1,552 were interested in purchasing consumer tech products or services this winter holiday season. Fieldwork was undertaken Sept. 3-6, 2026. The survey was carried out online. The figures have been weighted and are representative of all US adults (aged 18 and older).

In today's job market, do applicants really have a choice of whether to comply with AI hiring tools?

Hiring managers are more suspicious than ever of AI use in applications, and it’s impacting who they consider. At the same time, they’re turning to AI to help screen more candidates — meaning those videos you’ve seen on the internet of people pranking AI interviewers aren’t going away anytime soon.

New data from hiring systems firm Greenhouse found that “nine in ten US employers (90%) believe they’ve turned away real candidates because those applications seemed fake or AI-generated.” Greenhouse clarified that it doesn’t know whether employers are putting applications through AI detection tools or not.

Also: How many jobs is your state losing to AI? This dashboard tracks the cuts – and the cost

“The survey data is self-reported, so it reflects what employers believe has happened, not a measured outcome,” Greenhouse’s Head of Voice AI Ophir Samson told ZDNET via email.

Employers are also reacting to AI by adjusting their hiring processes: 86% of those surveyed reported changes to account for AI’s impact. 57% of them did so by adding another human interview.

“As jobseekers rely more on AI to polish and send out their job applications, employers are finding it harder to tell who’s actually right for the role,” the report stated, echoing an ongoing push-and-pull between applicants and hiring teams. AI resume screeners automatically toss a majority of applications they deem unfit, so applicants try not to get tossed by formatting their material for the screener, which then backfires anyway.

The report shows how a tough economy and an influx of AI hiring tools are colliding, arguably to benefit employers over applicants. Greenhouse noted that, ironically, AI tools are helping hiring managers while also making resumes untrustworthy, and applicants would rather be interviewed by AI than not at all.

Also: How to beat the AI algorithm and get the job of your dreams

“A growing number of employers are using AI not just to filter candidates out, but to have conversations with more candidates, earlier, through AI-powered voice technology,” Greenhouse said, adding that “half now use AI interviews to hear from more candidates, and 40% of those have found strong candidates they would have missed.”

Greenhouse itself offers a voice AI screening interview tool. Samson told ZDNET that an HR professional ran 200 candidates she’d rejected through Greenhouse’s tool, and it suggested 19.

“All five of the finalists came from that group, and she ultimately hired one from the group,” Samson said.

What we don’t, and maybe can’t, know is the inverse: whether AI screeners influence hiring managers to turn away candidates they actually should have considered. At least in Greenhouse’s case, Samson said Voice AI doesn’t make hiring decisions or “automatically advance, reject, or rank candidates.”

“Recruiters review every output, and one recruiter owns the outcome and can explain how they reached it,” he said.

Greenhouse’s report surveyed 1,347 hiring managers and recruiters across the US, UK, Germany, Australia, and Ireland from late September to mid-October, and found that half of employers using voice AI “say the early-stage candidate experience has improved.”

Also: ‘So perfect, they are literally identical’ – Your AI-polished resumes are recruiters’ new top stressor

It’s unclear what “improved” means there, though, and whether applicants themselves would agree with that. Still, when given the choice, only 7% of applicants in the US would turn down an AI interview, per an earlier Greenhouse report. Additionally, “70% of those who’ve had a live AI interview say it helped them show their skills,” that report said.

But how swayed is that by the state of the US job market? October’s job report was better than expected, but it’s still been a tough year overall for job-seekers. Greenhouse’s findings could be as much a reflection of how desperate applicants are as an endorsement of or comfort with AI screenings.

“The job market could be a factor. Our Future of Hiring Candidate Report shows 81% of job seekers were rejected from a job in the past year without speaking to anyone at the company, human or AI,” Samson said. “But I’d be careful about reading the data as desperation. Candidates are setting clear conditions: nearly half (49%) want to know if a human will review their responses and 40% want to know how they’ll be evaluated.”

Also: Why replacing staff with AI backfires – and 5 ways smart leaders generate real value instead

Samson said that a software engineer named Ryan Quinlan, who was hired at Blissway, initially thought “talking to an AI” sounded stranger, but that it ultimately “felt like a conversation” that let him mention skills he’d forgotten to include on his resume. Samson said that Ryan has been “a ‘maybe’ on paper,” but that the AI interview helped him get over the line to be considered.

“For most applicants, a human conversation was never on the table,” Samson said. “The real choice is a resume lost in a pile, or 15 minutes to tell their story.”

Greenhouse found that while employers are using AI to screen more candidates, most are maintaining human oversight over the most important decisions in the hiring process.

“Of all the tasks employers would hand to an AI agent, deciding which candidates to advance came last, at just 7%,” Greenhouse said.

A recent California law aims to protect employees from being fired by AI systems that make determinations about their performance without a human co-signing the assessment. As with many AI productivity tools in the workplace, proper adoption ideally equates to more time for human workers to handle more important tasks.

Also: 92% of HR say staff can train for AI jobs – but half of companies still hire outside

“Of employers who’ve saved time with AI, 85% put it back into candidates, most often by spending more time with shortlisted candidates (45%) and interviewing more candidates earlier (40%),” Greenhouse said.

The main question around AI interviewers remains whether they’re correctly capturing your interview the way you’d hope a human interviewer would (though that’s still deeply subjective and out of applicants’ control anyway).

“When AI interviews are implemented thoughtfully and transparently, they pay off for both candidates and recruiters,” Samson said. “Every candidate who uses our Voice AI can opt out, and about 90% rate the experience as excellent.”

#3113. "The Big Short's" Michael Burry Issued a Blunt Warning about Anthropic

Burry has made some pretty impressive short bets over the past two decades.

By Bram Berkowitz – Nov 19, 2026 at 4:28PM EST

10 stocks we like better than Anthropic ›

Dr. Michael Burry made a name for himself during the Great Recession in 2008, when, prior to the collapse of the housing bubble, he bet against mortgage-backed securities that would eventually fail, earning hundreds of millions of dollars in profits for him and the investors in his hedge fund.

Due to Burry's track record, the market still pays close attention to his investment calls. In recent weeks, he has issued a blunt warning about Anthropic (ANT +17.07%), which just went public Thursday.

Michael Burry. Image source: Getty Images.

Since the emergence of artificial intelligence and large language models (LLMs), Burry has largely been bearish on the AI revolution. At this point, he believes a bubble has formed in the industry, and that the market has gotten far too exuberant about the values of the companies involved in it.

As part of its IPO process, Anthropic had to disclose many details about the company's inner workings, including its financials. In the second quarter, it generated spectacular revenue growth of 144% sequentially to nearly $11.6 billion. The company even managed to generate an operating profit.

However, in the third quarter, revenue was nearly $17 billion. That nearly 47% sequential growth disappointed some onlookers because it slowed quarter over quarter, although it was still incredibly strong. Anthropic is a frontier AI lab, and its models have found strong resonance with enterprises. But there are now more open-weight models that are reportedly much cheaper to use.

"Not only is the company priced for optimism... it is betting its entire existence on that optimism," Burry wrote in a Substack post, according to Business Insider.

But Burry's even bigger concern has to do with the magnitude of the spending Anthropic has committed to on compute to power and train its models. Vast quantities of compute will really be required in perpetuity to support its business model. Anthropic said in its registration statement that it had already committed to spend roughly $895 billion on compute, a significant portion of which is projected to be spent by the end of 2030. This also doesn't include an additional $125 billion to $150 billion of compute the company plans to purchase between 2028 and 2031.

Burry noted that these commitments are equivalent to roughly 12 times the more bullish revenue estimates for Anthropic of about $100 billion over the next year. He also noted that while the market is not blind to what's going on, he doesn't believe investors are concerned enough, and he has no plans to invest in the stock.

"Under take-or-pay, Anthropic could end up effectively paying more for compute at a time when it is not needed, which would increase its costs and reduce competitiveness with other language model providers," he added.

Burry’s warning hits the question sitting at the crux of the debate over the AI trade: Is spending hundreds of billions of dollars annually — and soon-to-be trillions — going to yield adequate returns on investment?

Certainly, no one can scoff at Anthropic's product or its revenue growth, but its third-quarter results highlighted that its growth may not be linear, and it may slow from here.

Anthropic priced its IPO at $1.5 trillion. Annualizing Anthropic's third-quarter revenue of nearly $17 billion would give it an implied annual recurring revenue (ARR) run rate of $68 billion and a price-to-ARR multiple of about 220.

Bullish investors, of course, can be tempted to assume that revenue will keep growing like a weed, but we still don't fully know how competition from open-weight models will impact its business, nor how future innovations in the rapidly-evolving AI segment could potentially erode Anthropic's moat.

Burry's warning is that the company will have to spend hundreds of billions of dollars on data center compute, even as its growth trajectory remains uncertain. Furthermore, the cost it is paying for compute now may look high in several years.

That's why I think investors should remain on the sidelines in the coming months and gather more intel on Anthropic's business before deciding whether to buy the stock.

With temporary threads, any searches you run in Google’s AI Mode won’t be associated with your account or saved to your chat history.

New to Google’s AI Mode is an option known as temporary threads. By choosing this setting, any searches you conduct in AI mode are detached from your own Google account and history. Your temporary searches won’t be affected by your past preferences or chats. They won’t be impacted by any personalization you’ve set up through your account. And they won’t be saved to your chat history. The goal here is to prevent anyone else, including Google, from accessing your conversations in this mode.

This option is currently rolling out around the world in all languages to Google search on both desktop and mobile browsers. You can run a temporary thread on any device and in any browser.

Try this for yourself: Head to the regular Google search page and click the button on the search field for AI Mode. You should then see an icon with a pen hovering over a dotted circle. If you don’t see it, you may have to run a search to get started. On the results page, you should then spot the icon.

Hover over the icon, and the tooltip will say: “Start temporary thread.” Click the icon on the left to start a new thread. Now, any conversation you kick off will be temporary and unconnected to your account. But you don’t have to stick with just plain old text. Select the plus icon to upload an image or file. Google will still collect data and use data that is not associated with your account, including to keep our services working smoothly and safely and to support business operations.”

Google also warns that your browser may still save your history if you visit a website within a temporary thread. Data could still be collected by the sites you visit and the services those sites use, including Google services like Google Analytics.

#3106. I’ve tested countless Linux distros, and Pond is unlike anything I’ve tried – here’s why

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Tech > Services & Software > Operating Systems > Linux

Feeling adventurous? This Linux distribution is exciting, efficient and totally unique.

Linux is all about choice. From the kernel all the way up to the desktop environment, you get to determine what is used and even how it is used. The staggering number of distributions, desktops, package managers, file managers, and terminal apps provide you with a nearly infinite combination of choices. That choice is and has always been a key aspect of Linux.

Also: My favorite Linux desktop environment for laptops surprised even me

So too is innovation. If there’s one thing that separates Linux from all other operating systems, it’s the willingness to try something different. Linux developers are always pushing the limits of what an operating system is, and this new take on the OS is the epitome of that.

The distribution in question is called Pond. According to the developers, “Pond is an opportunity for us to play with familiar conventions and experiment with new ideas that make a computer more natural and satisfying.”

The developers have achieved something special. Pond takes the standard UI and turns it on its head. Part tiling window manager, part mobile UI, part GNOME, and part something we’ve never before seen, this desktop environment is special. It took me all of five minutes to fall in love with what they’ve created.

Also: The only 4 Linux email clients I recommend

If you’ve ever considered using a tiling window manager, but thought the lack of a mouse made it seem a bit too complicated, Pond is exactly what you want. Here’s how it works:

Pond uses the Niri window manager to arrange windows in columns along an infinite strip from left to right. In multi-monitor setups, each display gets its own strip, so windows never “overflow” from one monitor to the next.

Also: How to install Arch Linux without losing your mind

At the same time, workspaces are dynamic, and there’s always a new workspace automatically created to the right of the farthest-right window. The combination of the Pond sidebar and Niri’s way of handling windows makes this UI truly original.

Pond doesn’t have a traditional desktop menu. Instead, you open the launcher (using the Super+Space key combination), type the name of the app you want to install, and hit Enter when the app name appears on both the display and as an icon in the top portion of the sidebar.

Another thing that sets Pond apart is how you install apps. Yes, you can open a terminal window and install an app using the pacman command, or you can open the launcher, type install, press Enter, and then type the name of the app you want to install. For instance, if you wanted to install LibreOffice, you would type:

Once you hit Enter a second time, the installation will begin. Many apps install via Flatpak, but on the off-chance an app must be installed via the pacman package manager, you’ll be prompted to type your user password before the installation begins.

As I hinted earlier, Pond is based on Arch Linux, which means it’s a rolling-release distribution. One issue that did give me pause was the lack of a GUI update system, which indicates that updates would have to happen in the terminal, like so:

I installed the Shelly GUI frontend, which does have an update component. Personally, I would simply open the terminal window, type sudo pacman -Syu, hit Enter, and let the update run in the background. But if a GUI is your jam, Shelly is what you want.

Also: A super fast distro for anyone ready to move beyond beginner Linux

It would be sweet if the developers allowed updating the system from within the launcher, so it didn’t require opening the terminal first. The Pond launcher does allow running system commands from the launcher, which will then open the terminal window and execute the command. For instance, open the terminal, type a command, hit Enter, and then scroll through the list of available commands that can be run.

Pond ships with kernel 7.3.4-3, so it has outstanding hardware recognition and performance.

You should definitely give Pond a try, especially if you’re adventurous and want to experience something completely different. If, on the other hand, different is not in your stream, then Pond will frustrate you to no end.

Also: Why Nextcloud Office is my new favorite free productivity suite

Pond excited me more than any OS has in a very long time; so much so that I could see this becoming my go-to OS, once it reaches stable release. Until then, I will keep Pond installed on a laptop, keep upgrading, and see what happens next.

Kudos to the Pond OS team for coming up with something truly unique in an already competitive world.

#3104. Windows’ Baseline Protection Can Simplify Security, but There Could Be Pitfalls

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

It makes security a little easier to manage, but apps can also refuse to work if your machine fails security checks.

Microsoft’s collecting all of Windows 11’s hardware-related security features under one roof starting in 2027. Announced during its Ignite developer conference this week, in addition to seven new AI models, baseline protection is a way to make Windows more secure out of the box.

The combination of core security safeguards into a single pass-or-fail device status is a boon, but it may also introduce problems, including for gamers, who tend to tweak aspects of the operating system environment, like UEFI BIOS settings.

A Microsoft spokesperson told CNET in an email that baseline protection is still in the preview stage and that the company will “continue to iterate and build upon this based on the feedback the company hears from customers, partners and developers.”

Currently, Windows’ eight key hardware security features are spread across the OS: the Trusted Platform Module security processor, Memory Integrity (which prevents unwanted alternation of data in memory), Kernel debugger protection (to guard the core code of the OS), Secure Boot (which ensures no tampering during system startup), driver security and a few others.

To manage or check these settings, you have to visit multiple locations, and if app developers need to verify them at runtime, they have to perform similar gymnastics.

The upcoming functionality will consolidate all those settings into a single control panel within Windows’ Security settings section, where you’ll be able to check their status and apply any necessary updates. Since it tracks all eight security features, developers will only need to confirm that baseline protection is met.

The feature is currently available in Windows Insider builds and is expected to roll out to the general public in 2027.

Baseline protection provides instructions for enabling these features if they’re not readily available. For example, enabling Secure Boot requires restarting directly into your BIOS. To save you time, the panel provides step-by-step instructions right on the screen, so you don’t have to look up how to do it yourself.

Application developers may have the biggest win here. The ability to poll just one security feature instead of eight individual ones streamlines the development process and allows developers to check security features quickly and easily. For instance, game anti-cheat software relies on multiple security measures to verify that no third-party code is running.

Microsoft has 11 initial software partners, including heavy hitters like Adobe, 1Password, Blizzard and Epic Games, each of which is incorporating support to help it identify risk faster, including detecting counterfeit and malicious software.

“A consistent security signal gives apps and organizations a shared foundation to build on,” said Michael Draper, vice president of Global Consumer Trust at Adobe, in a testimonial.

Power users and gamers potentially stand to lose the most from this new feature. Many of them intentionally disable certain security settings to dual-boot Linux, run custom hardware drivers or improve gaming performance by disabling Virtualization-Based Security, which can lower frame rates and cause visual glitches.

Also, since developers can perform a single pass-fail check for all the settings, users may be shoehorned into keeping all eight features enabled, even if the developer doesn’t need them all.

Microsoft is leaving enforcement up to the developer, though. For example, an application may check baseline protection, see that it’s not fully satisfied, but allow a user to run it anyway with a warning screen or another pop-up or reminder. Alternatively, the software may refuse to run until the user enables full baseline protection.

“Windows baseline protection gives the app information on each security requirement, and developers can choose to enable some or all requirements,” said a Microsoft spokesperson. “Microsoft still recommends developers embrace all requirements to meet the strongest security bar.”

Adobe, Blizzard, 1Password and most of Microsoft’s other partners haven’t expressly said they’ll lock users out of apps without complaints, but a few have strongly hinted that this will be the case.

#3099. The Crypto Bear Market Could Be Back. Here’s What I’m Doing About It.

With Bitcoin's spectacular breakdown over the last weeks, a lot of questions about the crypto market's short-term prospects are being raised.

By Alex Carchidi – Nov 19, 2026 at 4:33PM EST

The crypto bear market may not be as completely finished as investors had hoped. After a weak October, between Nov. 5 and Nov. 17, Bitcoin (BTC -2.14%) fell about 19%, putting its price near $65,000 -- not too far from the $58,000 level it hit during the depths of the summer's doldrums. Other crypto market leaders like Ethereum (ETH -3.22%), Hyperliquid (HYPE -3.30%), Solana (SOL -2.50%), and Zcash (ZEC -9.31%) have been falling quickly too.

This pullback wasn't something I expected, but here's how I'm planning to make the most of it.

First, let's unpack a few headwinds blowing strongly at the moment.

October's hot inflation readout increased the odds of the Federal Reserve hiking interest rates at its December meeting, making bonds more tempting and assets that pay no interest, like most of crypto, less appealing to investors. Separately, the Democrats' incoming takeover of Congress is making the market more volatile due to a widespread (and not entirely accurate) expectation that Democrats are bad for asset prices.

As if that weren't enough, there's an ongoing sell-off in artificial intelligence (AI) stocks, which is depressing marketwide sentiment and has just gone into overdrive as a result of the Nvidia drama.

Then there's the collection of crypto-specific problems, most of which would be digested by the market as fairly routine if they weren't happening at the same time as the above.

Hackers stole $6.3 billion in funds from Binance in October. Then, as part of the ongoing sell-off, investors withdrew $1.3 billion from U.S. Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) in the week ending Nov. 6, with additional withdrawals in the subsequent week.

Finally, as marketwide selling accelerated on Nov. 15, about $2 billion in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated, sending the market lower.

One particularly concerning aspect of the ongoing downtrend is that positive news and good financial performance are not leading to consistent increases in the prices of leading assets.

For example, Hyperliquid runs a blockchain exchange for perpetual futures (perps), price-tracking contracts that never expire, and on Oct. 29, the New York Stock Exchange's parent company, Intercontinental Exchange, inked a deal to run new U.S. perps markets designed by TradeXYZ and built on Hyperliquid's technology, pending regulatory approval. As far as upside catalysts go, it's hard to imagine a better one for Hyperliquid than that.

Hyperliquid brought in $71.7 million in revenue in the 30-day period ending on Nov. 17. Yet the coin is now 29.2% below its all-time high set earlier this year. And the three Hyperliquid ETFs have had six straight weeks of net capital outflows through Nov. 13.

When investors sell a project that's making money and teeing up future income, it signals very low confidence, suggesting the crypto bear market never ended despite some excitement in the late summer.

I am taking this signal as an opportunity to reassess my read on the crypto market.

My prior analysis was that the bear market was over, due to the now-erased rebound in Bitcoin's price, the continued uptrends in Zcash, Hyperliquid, and Solana, and an explosion of new projects hosted on Solana and elsewhere. I calculated that their strong performance, both in their fundamentals and in price, would enable them to muddle through the uncertainty and headwinds I knew they were facing. That could still happen, but it's now less probable.

Instead, I'm now assessing that I should look for opportunities to slowly buy the dip in these assets with small amounts of capital, with the intention of holding whatever I buy for at least a handful of years. After all, the market could keep falling from here if the bear market really is back.

Even if it doesn't, the arrival of a new crypto bull market looks a lot further away than it did just a few months ago.

#3097. Meta Is Trying to Woo Teens to Instagram Through Schools

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Project Gryffindor is an initiative intended to make Instagram popular by marketing "school communities" on the platform.

Meta has justifiably attracted more scrutiny than ever this year, along with multibillion-dollar judgments and settlements, over how its business practices affect young social media users. The company, however, is not retreating.

In fact, the tech giant has made a major push toward drawing teenagers to one of its flagship platforms, Instagram, by targeting them at their schools.

According to documents obtained and reported by NPR, Meta launched an initiative called Project Gryffindor, named after a Hogwarts house in the Harry Potter series, to create school communities on Instagram in order to boost user counts and engagement on the platform.

Meta’s goal of approaching young users where they spend the most time offline was not a secret. As recently as late September, the company said it was expanding its School Partnership Program, which includes 17,000 schools, with a stated goal to “help students and parents stay informed.”

The company’s internal documents reveal some of the motivations behind Meta’s push for school adoption and Project Gryffindor’s proposed features, such as school banners on teen profiles and the ability to search school directories by class year. The details were acquired as part of discovery in a multistate lawsuit over whether social media platforms are designed to be addictive to users under 18. Meta is a defendant in the case, along with other companies, including TikTok, Snap and Google.

In 2024, Instagram introduced Teen accounts and has since been trying to assure parents they’re safe while rolling out additional protections. Studies, however, have suggested that young teens regularly encounter unsafe content or deal with unwanted contact. Recruiting more users at an early age without resolving these risks could make teens more vulnerable to mental health issues and increase the chances of being bullied or harassed.

A representative for Meta did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Like other social platforms, Instagram primarily makes its money from targeted advertising. User retention is a key part of Meta’s strategy.

In one of the document slides, titled “Why schools, why now?” which preceded Gryffindor’s launch, Meta said, “Competitors are exploring school social use cases, but IG may be better positioned for school connections thanks to our differentiator of meeting new people and building relationships with acquaintances.” In other words, Instagram’s size and scale, with about 3 billion active users globally, automatically make it a draw for students.

The NPR report comes within a week of a filing against Meta alleging that it’s withholding evidence in a major case involving social media’s effects on teenagers.

One of Meta’s marketing pitches for its School Partnership Program is that it’s trying to create online safe spaces for students, while giving parents and schools more oversight on what’s accessible on the platform. But experts warn that Meta’s history makes it hard to trust the company with protecting kids from predators or scammers.

Katie Paul, director of the Center for Accountability’s Tech Transparency Project, which has been researching how Meta handles child-safety issues, said that Instagram Teen accounts “are not safe as advertised” and that nothing is “legally requiring the company to make these safe.” Paul pointed out that Instagram launched these accounts only when lawsuits over social media harm started rolling in.

“It’s all part of a broader marketing (effort) to claim that these are just safer for kids because they are Teen accounts,” Paul said. That marketing effort has included paid endorsements from therapists, psychologists and parent influencers to promote Teen accounts. The case for building up partnerships with schools is a way of “passing the buck on responsibility” to schools and parents, Paul said.

Parents, in particular, have less power in Instagram’s school groups: Unlike the school administrators tasked with managing school groups, parents have no powers to moderate or manage those groups; they can only view them. For Teen accounts in general, parents can’t view direct messages sent to or received by their children.

Meta’s business interests in its push for student engagement and school partnerships are easy to see through. Because kids are likely to be lifetime users on these platforms, getting them hooked early has long-term financial value.

“Ultimately, Meta is the one profiting off of the data collection of these kids while simultaneously failing to keep them safe,” Paul said.

TL;DR: Mortgage rates eased today, but borrowing costs are still expensive for many homebuyers.

Mortgage rates are lower today, but recent averages above 7% are still eating into buyers’ budgets.

The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage dropped to 7.13% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 21 basis points lower than yesterday and 13 basis points higher than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.)

Here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context:

» Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders

Mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to new inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

On Friday, the Bureau of Labor Statistics released the Producer Price Index for October, which tracks the change in prices that U.S. producers are able to get for their products. This is one way to measure inflation on the market end, rather than the consumer end.

The results were mixed. While prices didn’t rise quite as high as economists anticipated month-over-month (0.3% vs. 0.4%), year-over-year price growth did reach 6.5% — the largest increase in four years. This points to even higher costs for consumers coming in the near future.

Investors are convinced that the Federal Reserve will raise overnight borrowing rates again in December to pull inflation down. And higher overnight borrowing rates — called the federal funds rate, which is what banks pay to fund products like mortgages — usually lead to higher mortgage rates.

» MORE: How the Federal Reserve affects mortgage rates

Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you plan to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

With rates where they are right now, you may want to start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.63% or higher.

Also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

» Time to refi? Compare refinance rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders

There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

If the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

NerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a new home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

» Is now a good time to buy? See NerdWallet’s analysis

If you already have a quote you’re happy with, you should consider locking your mortgage rate, especially if your lender offers a float-down option. A float-down lets you take advantage of a better rate if the market drops during your lock period.

Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

🤓 Nerdy Reminder: Rates can change daily, and even hourly. If you’re happy with the deal you have, it’s okay to commit.

#3093. GTA 6 Launch Day Hits Different for Fired Rockstar Workers

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Three people among the bigger group fired from Rockstar last year describe the "bittersweetness" of finally seeing the game they poured their hearts into out in the world.

As people across the world sneak a day away from the office to play the long-awaited Grand Theft Auto 6 on Thursday, the Rockstar employees who made the game are hopefully enjoying a well-earned day off in celebration. But not everyone who worked on the cultural juggernaut is joining the victory lap.

For the 34 workers based in the UK and Canada who Rockstar dismissed in October 2025, GTA 6 launch day isn’t the day of celebration it should’ve been.

“I should be with my team, taking a photo at every poster I can see, and be happy about it,” says Branimira Yordanova, who worked for three years in the lighting department at Rockstar North in Edinburgh, Scotland. “But it’s impossible because of how much hurt the firing has caused everyone.”

Rockstar fired the workers on the spot — something that’s only legal in the UK in cases of gross misconduct — alleging that they’d shared confidential company information on a Discord server.

The workers tell a different story. They say the company had long been aware of the Discord server, and only fired them when it started to look as though their efforts to unionize might succeed. They believe they were made an example of.

On the evening before the game’s launch, I spoke with Yordanova and her former colleague Dayne Oram, a senior production coordinator who had been at Rockstar North for seven years and was also affected by the dismissals, about how they were feeling about launch day.

“One of our fellow colleagues said it the best,” says Yordanova. “What we’ll feel tomorrow is mourning what could have been, whether we want to or not.”

For all those who are mourning, others among the fired workers still hold a candle for GTA. Jacob Jones, who spent one year as a game tester before taking a role as a designer on the open world team for four years, was raring to play the game on launch day.

Jones graduated from being a childhood fan of the franchise – even counting the signatures of Rockstar co-founders Sam and Dan Hauser among his merch collection – to his dream job. He remains a GTA fan to this day, but describes feeling a sense of “poignance” and “bittersweetness” toward the launch.

For Oram, Yordanova and Jones, GTA 6 eve was already a heavy day, even aside from the launch fever.

They’re all part of a case brought by the Independent Workers’ Union of Great Britain on behalf of 23 former Rockstar North employees, who say they were unfairly dismissed for union activity. Hours before Oram and Yordanova spoke with me, a Glasgow employment tribunal had heard Rockstar’s closing submissions, which now leaves the fired workers in limbo as they wait for a verdict.

Rockstar North maintains that it fired the employees for gross misconduct. The company didn’t respond to a request for further comment.

Oram, Yordanova and Jones all speak highly of their former colleagues and teams, but Oram calls the sacking a “traumatic experience.” None have managed to secure alternative employment in the past 13 months. Jones says for now he’s focused on getting justice.

Meanwhile, reminders of their former employer have been everywhere as the studio geared up to release perhaps the most highly anticipated game of all time. Billboards, buses and online ads have been impossible to avoid, leaving Yordanova feeling “devastated.”

“I’ve genuinely had to make sure to avoid looking at it,” she says. “It’s such a cool game, and to know that you worked on it, you feel a sense of pride and joy to see it out. But it’s like that sense of joy has been taken away from us in such a ruthless manner.”

Oram acknowledges having “mixed feelings” about the launch. It’s been fantastic watching video footage of people playing and reviewing the game, they say. At the same time, they’ve found it difficult not being able to celebrate the moment with their former team.

The workers fired from Rockstar North had varying ideas about whether they wanted to celebrate the launch, or avoid it entirely. Jones is one of those who started playing the game as soon as he got home from the tribunal at 1 a.m. By the time we spoke on Thursday, he’d played around six or seven hours.

“I personally think it’s a masterpiece,” he says. Even though he worked on the game, he’s discovering surprises everywhere. “I haven’t completed it yet, but I do think it is probably the greatest game ever made.”

Oram says that they planned to stick with watching streams of the game on launch day. “I’m probably not going to play the game for a little while, but I am looking forward to at least watching some people,” they say. Oram worked across so many bits of the game that there’s plenty they’re excited to see people discover.

Yordanova says she’s firmly in the avoidance camp. “I was really excited about playing the game in its official form because obviously when you work on it, you get to play it,” she says. “Even while we were in the office, there were parts I was really excited about – but I don’t think I’ll be playing it for the foreseeable future.”

She hopes that one day her feelings will change, she adds. “But right now, that’s just not possible in any way.”

Instead, she’ll be spending the day with friends who supported her over the last year. She plans to “dive into another art form” by seeing the stop-motion animated film Wildwood at the cinema, which particularly appeals to her as a lighting artist.

Many people playing GTA 6 around the world won’t be aware of what happened to Oram, Yordanova, Jones and their colleagues during the game’s development, but the affected workers would like people to know. “I understand people just want to focus on the joy, but I don’t think you can separate the launch with what happened,” says Yordanova.

Reflecting on what happened, Jones says it’s such a shame the way things went down. “It was my absolute passion,” he says. “I just wish that the circumstances were different, and I would have loved to have still been there working on games. I wish I got to the end.”

#3092. 22nd Century (XXII) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Consumer pack sales for Pinnacle VLN surged as the branded pivot took hold.

By Motley Fool Transcribing – Nov 19, 2026 at 4:40PM EST

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

22nd Century (XXII +7.54%) reported a transition toward a branded-product strategy, emphasizing its FDA-authorized low-nicotine offerings. Management indicated that the company is shifting its manufacturing focus away from low-margin contract work to prioritize higher-tier branded products like Pinnacle VLN and Pinnacle Pure. The company completed a restructuring of its capital table to remove warrant overhang and facilitate future growth financing. Strategic initiatives include expanding direct-to-consumer reach through digital platforms and increasing the retail footprint across authorized states.

Operator: Welcome to the 22nd Century Group's third quarter 2026 conference call and webcast. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. It is now my pleasure to turn the call over to Daniel Otto, Chief Financial Officer of 22nd Century Group. Please go ahead.

Daniel Otto: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to 22nd Century Group's third quarter 2026 earnings conference call. Thank you for joining us. With me on the call today is Lawrence Firestone, Chief Executive Officer. Before we begin, please note that today's remarks include forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those described in these statements. Please refer to the company's earnings release and SEC filings, including our most recent annual report on Form 10-K and quarterly reports on Form 10-Q, for a discussion of these risks and other factors. In addition, during today's call, management may refer to certain non-GAAP financial measures.

Reconciliations of those measures to the most directly comparable GAAP measures are included in the company's earnings release. With that, I'll go through the financial results first, then turn the call over to Lawrence to discuss broader corporate updates and highlights. Let me start with the P&L headline. Net revenues for the third quarter were $4.8 million, up 66% from $2.9 million in the second quarter 2026, and up 18.6% from $4 million in the third quarter of 2025. For the first nine months of 2026, net revenues were $11.7 million versus $14.1 million in the prior year period. The decline year-over-year is consistent with the planned exit of low and negative margin contract volume.

Sales by product line for the quarter were cigarette revenues of $3.9 million versus $2.3 million in the second quarter on higher cartons sold and better pricing. Filtered cigar revenues were $0.7 million, consistent with the second quarter, as that category continues its planned wind-down. Other tobacco products contributed $0.1 million compared to -$0.2 million in the second quarter, of which the prior quarter had included a one-time write-off of aged inventory discontinued by a customer. VLN cigarette revenues were $0.03 million, consistent with the second quarter, reflecting steady initial orders and reorders of Pinnacle VLN, alongside targeted price promotions that we view as awareness investments. These are promotions that are showing up in point-of-sale results at retail.

Continuing on, gross profit for the third quarter 2026 was +$0.4 million versus a gross loss of $0.3 million last quarter. The drivers are the ones we have described and are integral to our strategy, better mix and better pricing. Operating expenses for the third quarter 2026 were $3 million, flat sequentially. On a year-over-year basis, operating expenses are higher than the $2.2 million we recorded in the third quarter of 2025, which reflects deliberate investment in the commercial organization, including sales coverage, marketing execution, and the infrastructure required to service a larger and more demanding retail footprint. Operating loss for the third quarter 2026 narrowed to $2.6 million from $3.3 million last quarter.

Net loss from continuing operations was $2.6 million versus $3.3 million last quarter. Adjusted EBITDA loss improved to $2.2 million from a loss of $3.5 million last quarter. For the nine-month period, Adjusted EBITDA loss was $8.3 million versus $7.8 million in the prior year period, with the modest unfavorable variance reflecting the commercial investments I just described. On the balance sheet, we ended the quarter with $3.9 million of cash and no debt. Subsequent to quarter end, our at-the-market facility generated approximately $5.8 million of net proceeds, of which $1.2 million was used to redeem an equal amount of Series B convertible preferred shares at par, leaving us with approximately $8 million of cash on a pro forma basis.

One structural change to the cap table worth noting: as of September 30th, 2026, no warrants to purchase common stock remain outstanding. That entire class of dilution overhang is gone. The result is a capital structure that is dramatically simpler than the one we started 2026 with, as we look toward new capital raise going toward the commercial plan rather than toward servicing legacy structures. Looking at the fourth quarter, the financial agenda continues to focus on broadening distribution and increasing rate of sale. We expect to see the legacy CMO wind-down substantially complete by the end of 2026. These two forces will yield a new look in the P&L to our revenue run rate and growth going forward.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Lawrence.

Lawrence Firestone: Thanks, Daniel, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today and for your continued interest in 22nd Century Group. We continue to make significant progress towards our ultimate objective, becoming a pure-play tobacco company focused on leading the low-nicotine movement, anchored by our FDA-authorized low-nicotine cigarette products, Pinnacle VLN and our flagship VLN. We took an important step towards achieving this objective in the third quarter. Retail same-store sales reported by our retail partners for our Pinnacle Pure branded products, Pinnacle VLN and Pinnacle Pure, increased 166% compared to the previous quarter. More importantly, as our higher-margin branded products gain traction in the marketplace and consumers increasingly seek them out, our gross margin profile is improving significantly.

Pinnacle Pure, Pinnacle VLN, and our flagship VLN are positioned in the higher margin tiers of the tobacco market, where gross margins of 50% or more are achievable at scale. As sales volumes increase and we experience greater absorption of our manufacturing overhead, we believe we can achieve the gross margins, operating margins, and cash flow characteristics traditionally associated with the tobacco industry. We are now firmly in growth mode. With our branded products in the marketplace and generating sales, our primary focus is expanding distribution and increasing retail sales velocity. We now have meaningful in-market sales data that demonstrates consumer demand and provides us with the evidence needed to approach additional retailers and expand our distribution footprint.

Our two brands, Pinnacle and our flagship VLN brand, serve distinct consumer segments. Pinnacle VLN and our flagship VLN appeal to smokers who are actively looking for an alternative that allows them to continue smoking while reducing their nicotine consumption. Consumers who have discovered our low nicotine products are responding positively to the experience and are increasingly seeking out these products. The science supporting our VLN technology is well established, and we continue to hear directly from consumers across the U.S. who contact us through our tryvln.com website to find out where they can purchase our products. Unfortunately, some interested consumers live in states where we have the necessary state-level authorizations, but have not yet established retail distribution.

Our planned expansion through Gopuff is designed to help address this gap. Many of these consumers live in major metropolitan markets where Gopuff's direct-to-consumer platform can provide access to our products before we establish a broader brick-and-mortar retail presence. We also expect the resulting regional sales data to help us demonstrate local consumer demand and support our efforts to secure additional retail distribution in those markets. We believe low nicotine cigarette category is emerging as a meaningful segment of the tobacco market. Consumer interest is growing, and our products are positioned to serve smokers who want to change their nicotine consumption without necessarily switching to vaping products, e-cigarettes, or nicotine pouches.

We conducted a recent study involving more than 1,000 smokers, and over 70% of the respondents indicated they would like to change their smoking habits and reduce their nicotine consumption while continuing to smoke cigarettes. The study also identified similar interest among consumers who currently use vaping products and nicotine pouches. These findings reinforce our belief that there is a substantial consumer population seeking alternatives within the existing nicotine marketplace. We believe our VLN products offer an important option for these consumers. We are not simply introducing another cigarette brand. We are building a brand platform around a specific consumer need.

One recent customer experience illustrates the level of interest that we are beginning to see in our low nicotine products. A smoker for 50 years, after learning about our VLN products online, set out to address her nicotine cravings. In her words exactly, and I quote, "I did not want the nicotine to take over my life again." End quote. She then traveled approximately two hours each way to purchase our VLN cigarettes from one of our retail locations. Following her experience, she took the additional step of submitting a testimonial, including the quote I just read, through the FDA website, describing her satisfaction with the product.

Stories like this and others that are coming in demonstrate the importance of the product accessibility and the potential demand that can develop as consumer awareness increases. Pinnacle Pure serves a different consumer segment. The brand is designed to appeal to value-conscious smokers who are looking for an affordable alternative to traditional lower-priced cigarette brands. By offering a tobacco and water cigarette formulation in both regular and menthol varieties, we believe Pinnacle Pure provides consumers with a differentiated value proposition. Rather than relying exclusively on temporary discounts or coupons, we are offering a competitively priced product that consumers can choose as their regular brand.

In the approximately three and a half months since its market introduction, Pinnacle Pure has generated encouraging consumer response. Early retail performance indicates that consumers are willing to try the brand and that repeat interest is growing the brand. Our satisfied customer base is growing month-over-month, and we believe Pinnacle Pure has the potential to become a meaningful contributor to both revenue and gross margin as distribution expands. At this stage, our growth strategy is increasingly about execution. We currently have retail presence in 23 states through the nation's third-largest cigarette retailer. Our products are available in every store within that retailer's network, where we have the necessary state authorization. Establishing this relationship was an important proof of concept.

Successfully entering the distribution network of a major national retailer required considerable effort, but we have accomplished that milestone, and we are now positioned to build on it. Our next priority is expanding the distribution through the nation's second-largest cigarette retailer, where we currently have a presence in Illinois. We are actively working to expand into additional territories within this retailer's network. We are also preparing to launch Pinnacle VLN and Pinnacle Pure through the national direct-to-consumer platform, Gopuff, featuring home delivery of our products. We expect this initiative to begin in the fourth quarter, with the objective of establishing a well-developed direct-to-consumer operating model as we enter 2027.

Gopuff offers an important opportunity to reach consumers in markets where we have not yet established brick-and-mortar distribution. We believe this channel can accelerate product availability, generate valuable sales data, and help us demonstrate brand performance with consumer demand metrics to prospective retail partners. Our strategy is straightforward: expand distribution, increase sales velocity, educate the smoking consumer about our low-nicotine VLN products, build brand awareness, and establish a growing base of repeat customers. The U.S. tobacco market represents approximately $70 billion in annual sales, with cigarettes accounting for roughly $50 billion. Based on the reported research and industry reports over the past several years, more than 70% of smokers are interested in changing their habits.

Therefore, we believe the serviceable addressable market, or what I call SAM, we are targeting for our products is approximately $35 billion annually. Our ability to capture a meaningful share of that SAM will depend on consumer adoption and continued execution. We believe our VLN products are well-positioned within this opportunity. We have developed the only FDA-authorized low-nicotine combustible cigarette currently available in the United States, and consumer feedback regarding taste and the overall smoking experience has been all positive. Our objective is to make these products available in every state where they are authorized and available in as many of the more than 272,000 U.S. retail locations that sell cigarettes as possible.

We believe there is a sustainable place for low-nicotine cigarettes in this marketplace. The opportunity now is to accelerate retailer adoption, increase consumer awareness, and expand availability. As awareness of our VLN products continues to grow, we are receiving an increasing number of inquiries from prospective customers across the country, as well as from consumers outside the United States. Our marketing team, under new leadership, is developing programs designed to educate consumers, strengthen brand awareness, and support continued retail expansion. Importantly, the retail sales data that we have accumulated over the past year provides us with valuable insight into customer behavior and purchasing patterns.

With continued access to point-of-sale information, we can better understand the demographics and preferences of the markets we serve, and this allows us to tailor our marketing strategies to individual markets rather than relying on a one-size-fits-all approach. Our research and development team also continues to advance new tobacco technologies and product concepts. We are evaluating additional branded products designed to fit within the applicable regulatory framework, including cigarette predicate requirements established under the 2007 legislation and our existing MRTP and PMTA regulatory strategies. We believe our continued investment in product development, particularly in the low-nicotine combustible category, differentiates 22nd Century within the U.S. tobacco industry. Consumers interested in locating our VLN products can visit our store locator at tryvln.com.

We have also made substantial progress on the capital structure and financial fronts. The increased trading activity in our stock during October provided an opportunity to complete an important cleanup of our capitalization table. With the exception of one remaining preferred stockholder holding Series B preferred shares, our capital structure consists of only common stock now. We have also eliminated the outstanding warrant overhang, which significantly simplifies our capitalization structure. Additionally, we have addressed the applicable baby shelf limitations, making our $250 million shelf registration statement available for use without restrictions. These actions provide greater financial flexibility as we pursue our growth strategy.

We currently have sufficient cash on the balance sheet to fund operations well into 2027 based on management's current outlook, and our focus is on achieving cash flow breakeven before the additional capital becomes needed. Our priorities are clear: grow revenue, improve gross margins, manage operating expenses, and strengthen the balance sheet. Every pack and carton sold represents an opportunity to gain market share from established competitors and build a lasting relationship with a consumer seeking an alternative in their comfort zone with a cigarette. Our sights are set on the substantial market opportunity represented by consumers who are looking for solutions addressing nicotine and tobacco products.

Consumer preferences continue to evolve, and we believe many traditional cigarette smokers will consider VLN products as an alternative to switching to vaping products, e-cigarettes, or nicotine pouches. We are building our business around the idea that consumers want choices. An interesting example of this strategy can be found in the beer industry, particularly at Heineken. Heineken has successfully developed a portfolio of premium brands, and while introducing Heineken 0.0 to provide consumers with an additional choice, offering a zero-alcohol product within its flagship brand family. We see a similar opportunity with the Pinnacle brand platform and our flagship VLN products. Pinnacle Pure offers a differentiated tobacco and water product, while Pinnacle VLN provides a low-nicotine alternative.

Together, these products allow us to serve distinct consumer preferences within the combustible cigarette category. We believe the U.S. market presents a significant opportunity for this approach. The potential $35 billion SAM is substantial, and particularly when compared with the existing markets for vaping and smokeless nicotine tobacco products. Consumer migration towards alternative products is already underway. While adoption of low-nicotine cigarettes is still developing, we believe awareness is increasing and the opportunity to expand distribution is significant. Our competitive position is supported by our VLN technology, our FDA authorization, our established manufacturing capabilities, and our growing retail relationships.

The next phase is about execution and getting our products into more stores, making them easier for consumers to find, and building the sales momentum necessary to support sustainable growth. As we look towards the end of 2026 and into 2027, we believe 22nd Century Group is entering a new chapter. The restructuring work is substantially behind us. Our capital structure is simplified, our branded products are established in the marketplace, and we've begun building the retail relationships necessary to support national expansion. We now have a clear path forward with a focus on growing distribution, increasing sales, improving margins, and ultimately achieving cash flow breakeven.

Our goal is to establish 22nd Century as the leading company in the emerging low-nicotine cigarette category while continuing to develop innovative tobacco products that respond to changing consumer preferences. We believe Pinnacle Pure and Pinnacle VLN have meaningful opportunities within the approximately $50 billion U.S. cigarette market. We're excited about the progress we've made and the opportunities that lie ahead, and the potential to build a profitable, cash-positive, sustainable business in a mature industry. I would like to thank our employees, our management team, board of directors, retail partners, and shareholders for their continued commitment and support. We appreciate your interest in 22nd Century Group. Thank you for joining us today, and have a nice day.
